#6.1 Global flags

These flags work with all commands.

FlagDefaultMeaning
--namepghaCluster name. Lower-case letters, digits and -.
--tokenHCLOUD_TOKENHetzner API token.
--state-dir.Folder of pgha.db and of old *.pgha.json files.
--modelocalWhere state lives: local or remote (not available yet). Also PGHA_MODE.
--db<state-dir>/pgha.dbSQLite state file. Also PGHA_DB.
--ssh-identitynonePrivate key file for commands that use SSH.

#6.2 Cluster flags

estimate, up and adopt accept these flags.

FlagDefaultMeaning
--server-typecx33Server type for each node.
--locationsfsn1,nbg1,hel1One location for each node. Use 3, 5 or 7.
--volume-gb1000Data volume size for each node (10 to 10000).
--pg-version17PostgreSQL major version (14 to 18).
--imageubuntu-24.04Server image.
--lb-typelb11Load balancer type.
--lb-locationfirst locationLoad balancer location.
--public-lboffGive the load balancer a public address.
--ssh-key-namenoneName of an SSH key that is already in Hetzner.
--ssh-public-key~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pubPublic key file to upload.
--ssh-allow0.0.0.0/0,::/0Source ranges that can use SSH.
--tailscaleoffJoin Tailscale and close public SSH.
--networknoneName or ID of an existing private network. The cluster joins it and does not create one.
--keep-on-failureoffup and adopt only. Keep this run's new resources when creation fails.
--pgbounceroffRun PgBouncer on each node.
--pool-size20PgBouncer server connections for each database (1 to 150).
--backup-endpointnoneS3 endpoint host name.
--backup-bucketnoneS3 bucket. This turns backups on.
--backup-regionfirst label of the endpointS3 region.
--backup-keep-full2Number of full backups to keep.
--backup-max-gb(keep + 1) x volumeBackup storage size used for the bill.
--s3-base-price6.49Object storage base price for each month, net.
--s3-price-per-tb6.49Price for each extra TB for each month, net.
--s3-included-gb1000Storage included in the base price.

All locations must be in one Hetzner network zone. The default locations are all in eu-central.

#6.3 pgha estimate

Shows the estimated monthly bill. It creates nothing. It reads live prices from the Hetzner API, so it needs the token.

#6.4 pgha up

Creates the cluster.

  1. It shows the bill.
  2. It asks for confirmation. --yes skips the question.
  3. It creates the SSH key, network, firewall, volumes, servers and load balancer. --network skips network creation and uses that network.
  4. It writes the state file.

You can run up again. It skips the resources that exist. It does not change resources that exist.

If a step fails after retries, up deletes the resources that this run created, newest first, and then stops with the error. It never deletes:

  • resources that existed before this run, for example the nodes of a cluster that you grow, or a run that completes an earlier one;
  • a network you gave with --network;
  • an adopted server. adopt removes the labels it added and detaches the server from a network it attached.

The cleanup also runs after Ctrl+C. It has 15 minutes. If a delete fails, the error names it and says to run pgha down. --keep-on-failure keeps the new resources, for example to look at a failed server.

The load balancer joins the private network before up adds the nodes as targets. A run that completes an earlier one attaches an existing load balancer that has no network.

--monitor installs the alert timer on nodes created in this run. Read section 16. If a node already exists, up still succeeds and prints:

monitor installs on new nodes; run pgha monitor install

The servers install the software after up returns. This takes about 5 minutes. Use pgha status to see when the roles show primary and replica.

#6.5 pgha adopt

Builds the cluster around an existing server. Read section 17.

FlagMeaning
--serverName of the existing Hetzner Cloud server. Required.
--extra-packagesExtension packages to install on the new nodes.
--monitorInstall the alert timer. Read section 16.
--keep-on-failureKeep this run's new resources when creation fails.
--yesSkip the confirmation.

adopt rejects the backup flags and --pgbouncer.

#6.6 pgha status

Shows each node with its location, server status, role, addresses, SSH host and volume size. It also shows the load balancer addresses.

The role comes from the load balancer health checks:

RoleMeaning
primaryThe node is the leader.
replicaThe node is a healthy replica.
startingNo health check is green yet.

#6.7 pgha down

Deletes the load balancer, servers, firewall, network and the SSH key that the tool created. A network passed with --network is not deleted.

FlagMeaning
--delete-volumesAlso delete the data volumes. All data is lost.
--yesSkip the confirmation.

Without --delete-volumes, the volumes stay and continue to cost money.

down is blocked when the cluster has an adopted server.

#6.8 pgha db

CommandMeaning
db create <database>Create a database and its login. Print the connection strings.
db import <database>Create a database, then copy data from another server.
db listList the databases with size, limit and connection string.
db syncSend the connection limits to PgBouncer on all nodes again.
db drop <database>Delete a database and its login.
FlagCommandsMeaning
--publicallUse the public load balancer address in the connection strings.
--connections Ncreate, importConnection limit for this project (1 to 150).
--from URLimportSource database URL.
--yesdropSkip the confirmation.

Database names use lower-case letters, digits and _. The first character is a letter. The names postgres, replicator, template0 and template1 are reserved.

#6.9 pgha backup

CommandMeaning
backup runStart a backup on the leader.
backup listShow the stored backups and the WAL range.
backup checkTest WAL archiving and the repository.

backup run --type accepts auto, full, diff or incr. auto makes a full backup on Sunday and a differential backup on other days.

#6.10 pgha monitor

CommandMeaning
monitor installInstall or update the alert timer on every reachable node.

Read section 16 for the checks, the webhook body, and the threshold flags. There is no monitor run command and no monitor disable command.

#6.11 pgha console

Starts the web console. It prints a link with an access token.

FlagDefaultMeaning
--listen127.0.0.1:7070Address and port. 0.0.0.0:7070 opens it to the network.
--access-tokenrandomLogin token. Also PGHA_CONSOLE_TOKEN.
--ssh-public-key~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pubKey for new clusters when the form has none.

The global flags --token, --state-dir, --db, --mode and --ssh-identity apply too. --name has no effect; the console lists all clusters.

PageDoes
ClustersAll clusters with a pgha-cluster label, their health and running operations.
New clusterThe up form, with the live bill.
DashboardConnection string per database, read-write or read-only. Nodes and load balancer. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
Databasesdb list, db create, db import, db drop, db sync.
Backupsbackup list, backup run, backup check.
Monitoringmonitor install, with the saved thresholds.
OperationsLive log of each background task.
Settingsdown, with or without the volumes.

Health is healthy when there is one primary and all nodes are running and in the load balancer, degraded with one primary and fewer healthy nodes, and unavailable with no primary.

Create, delete, import, backup and alert tasks run in the background, one at a time per cluster. Their time limits are the same as the CLI. When you stop the console with Ctrl+C, it waits for the running tasks.

The task history goes into the operations table, so it stays after a restart. The log is saved every 2 seconds while a task runs. A task that was running when the console died shows as failed at the next start.

The JSON API is under /api/. Each call needs the session cookie or Authorization: Bearer <token>. Requests that change data must come from the same origin. A delete needs ?confirm=<name>.
These flags work with all commands.
